fieldValues.title: 6. Build: what we tried and where we went too far
fieldValues.thinking_reached:
The ideal: The change is made once, in the layer that owns it, in a clean workspace against the right build, and is not lost.

What we have tried: scripts/wt worktrees; pinned CLI builds and srs-pinned; the stale-sibling rule (srs-rust#874); capability layering and ADR-048; the revision-bump choreography; the MCP tool-first rule against mimicry; the release-plan practice from the RFC-051/052 retrospective.

Problems recorded here: SP-08, SP-28, SP-77, SP-30, SP-01, SP-49.
fieldValues.tensions:
- Line 1, Prepare the workspace and ship the change: too far toward Ship the change. About 115 stale worktrees of 140 (work-flow audit); on 2026-10-25 a report was built from a local srs-rust 240 commits behind master.
- Line 2, Compatibility and a clean cut: too far toward both compatibility and clean cut, by turns. RFC-051 and RFC-052 took 45 PRs, 9 repositories and 9 releases over 2 days 21 hours (retrospective); hand-written client types drift (programme cube, corner deliver, compatibility, adapter).
- Line 3, Fix it where you are and fix it once in the core: too far toward Fix where you are. Programme code is scattered and bound to one programme (SP-49); the site and essay editors wrote each document operation twice (srs-web#601).
fieldValues.unresolved_questions:
- The three tensions are a first pass: none has its four 2×2 cases or the cube filled yet (handbook, A domain's axes, steps 3 and 4).
- Is each tension orthogonal to the other two in this stage, and which pole is yang here: does it flip from the parent domain?
fieldValues.next_action: Fill the 2×2 cases from the stage's own history; then name the remedy that moves us back out of each shadow.
